807.1 Passenger car under 3,500 kg. The symbol stands for a car under 3,500 kg intended mainly for carrying goods or passengers.
807.2 Goods vehicle. The symbol stands for a vehicle intended for carrying goods, with a permitted total weight of more than 3.5 tonnes and for a maximum of eight passengers.
807.21 Goods handling. The symbol stands for the loading and unloading of heavy or bulky goods.
807.3 Bus. The symbol stands for a bus intended for more than 8 passengers.

807.4 Goods vehicle with trailer, vehicle combination. The symbol stands for a combination of a vehicle and a trailer, where the vehicle is intended for carrying goods, with a permitted total weight of more than 3.5 tonnes and for a maximum of eight passengers (goods vehicle).
807.51 Tractor. The symbol stands for tractors and work machines.
807.52 Tracked off-road vehicle. The symbol stands for a motor vehicle intended mainly for carrying people or goods off-road and fitted with tracks.
807.6 Bicycle. The symbol stands for a bicycle as defined in the traffic law.

807.65 Powered scooter. The symbol stands for a small motor vehicle that is not classed as a light moped and is designed for speeds from 6 km/h up to 25 km/h, e.g. a powered scooter and a two-wheeled vehicle on one axle. Such vehicles must not be driven on the carriageway.
807.71 Light moped. The symbol stands for a light moped as defined in the traffic law.
807.72 Motorcycle. The symbol stands for a motorcycle as defined in the traffic law.
807.81 Pedestrians. The symbol stands for pedestrian traffic.
807.82 Disabled road users. The symbol stands for traffic of disabled road users.
807.91 Motorhome. The symbol stands for motorhomes.
807.92 Caravans, folding caravans and trailer tents. The symbol stands for touring caravans such as caravans, folding caravans and trailer tents.

840.2 Hearing impaired road users. This sign draws attention to the fact that hearing impaired people may be expected in traffic.
842.1 Newly laid surface. This sign indicates that you are driving on a newly laid surface.
842.2 End of asphalt. This sign indicates that the paved surface ends and a gravel road begins.
844.1 Slow road. This sign indicates that you are driving onto a route that is passable for cars but is slow and possibly rough and steep.

844.2 Difficult road. This sign indicates that you are driving onto a route that is impassable for ordinary cars but passable for four-wheel-drive vehicles that are higher than ordinary cars, such as jeeps.

844.3 Demanding track. This sign indicates that you are driving onto a route that is passable only for specially equipped off-road vehicles, such as jeeps and mountain trucks. The route may have very steep hills, snow patches and rivers that are barely passable for vehicles.
846.3 Unbridged rivers. This sign indicates that you are driving onto a route with unbridged rivers that may be hazardous.

848.3 Snow on the road. This sign indicates that you are driving onto a route where impassable conditions may be expected and which may be passable only for larger or specially equipped jeeps and mountain trucks. The route may have steep hills and snow patches.
848.5 Slippery when wet. This sign indicates conditions that must be particularly guarded against in rain and wet weather.
850.1 Blind summit. This sign indicates that a rise that severely limits visibility is ahead.
850.2 Blind summit. This sign indicates that a rise that severely limits visibility is ahead.
852 Accident area. This sign indicates that accidents are unusually frequent in the area.
854.1 Single-track surface. This sign indicates that the paved surface is 5 metres wide or narrower. Road users must therefore move out onto the gravel shoulder when they meet.
854.2 Single-track bridge. This sign indicates that a single-track bridge is ahead.
854.3 Single-track bridge with a narrow carriageway. This sign indicates that a single-track bridge with a carriageway narrower than 3.05 m is ahead.
854.4 Single-track tunnel. This sign indicates that a single-track tunnel is ahead.
860 Chain-up area. This sign indicates a lay-by by the road intended specifically for drivers who need to fit or remove chains.
